Consult Summary:
- 32-year-old female presents with acute onset, severe unilateral headache, blurred vision with visual phenomena, dizziness, nausea, and vomiting. Clinical features suggest first episode of migraine.  

History:
- Presenting complaint: Severe headache started suddenly this morning; onset approximately 4 hours ago.
- Character: Unilateral (left side), not clearly described as behind the eye; intensity rated 6/10 (reference pain: kidney stones rated at 10/10).
- Associated symptoms: Blurry vision with zigzag lines, dizziness, nausea, vomiting (twice at onset), and intolerance of screens.
- Temporal profile: Symptoms began suddenly and have remained severe; some reported improvement in vision but ongoing headache and nausea.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Movement and getting out of bed worsen symptoms; keeping head still preferred. Paracetamol (acetaminophen) taken ~3 hours after onset was ineffective.
- Other relevant negatives: No previous similar headaches; no limb weakness; gait unaffected.
- Systems review: No limb weakness, no gait disturbance, no other neuro deficits reported.

Past Medical History:
- History of kidney stones.
- No regular medications.
- No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Not mentioned.

Family History:
- Mother has migraines and hypothyroidism.

Physical Examination:
- Not documented.

Investigations:
- None performed or documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute severe unilateral headache with visual disturbance, nausea, and vomiting—presumed first migraine episode.
  - Recommended trial of ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Suggested adding an anti-sickness medication (specific drug not specified).
  - Advised drinking sugary, carbonated beverages (e.g., Coke).
  - Advised monitoring response; if symptoms resolve before scheduled assessment, appointment can be canceled.
  - Instructed to seek urgent evaluation for any new or worsening symptoms (e.g., new neurological deficits) or no improvement.

- Issue 2: Assessment for other causes of acute headache (e.g., brain tumor, stroke) discussed due to patient concern.
  - Will arrange in-person assessment with full neurological exam if symptoms do not improve or as a safety net.

General plan items:
- Patient advised on red flag symptoms and to contact clinic for worsening or new symptoms.
- Safety netting discussed.

● Missing/expected elements: No documentation of vital signs, physical examination, detailed social history, or formal neurological examination. Medication/dose details not specified.
● Internal conflicts: None identified.
● Transcript quality: Transcript clear and complete; minimal technical interruption did not impact clinical content.
